title: Mool
question: Where should visual richness stop?
gap: The brand and product sections show the result without exposing the boundary between expression and financial clarity.

states.title: Use illustration to establish familiarity.
states.explain: Regional visual references frame the invitation to begin. They communicate belonging before the user has learned the interface.
states.trade: Extending this vocabulary needs cultural judgment, not just reusable components.
labels: The action still needs a plain label

states.title: Keep the money visually unambiguous.
states.explain: Amounts, dates and progress must remain easy to distinguish from the expressive surrounding artwork. This is the useful tension in the system.
states.trade: The case study identifies dense financial screens as an unresolved part of the two-voice system.

states.title: Start with a life question, then show a plan.
states.explain: “Can I send my kid to her dream school?” translates a financial product into an intention someone already has. Pair the question with the actual planning screen.
states.trade: The documented paced approach costs experienced users extra steps.

title: M Health Fairview
question: What can a patient answer before knowing the service names?
gap: The audit and constraints are pitch-deck slides; the page does not visually connect each finding to the new information architecture.
insert: Replace the opening audit / before-and-after sequence.

states.title: Service categories make the patient decode the system.
states.explain: Urgent care, virtual urgent care and eVisit are service names. The documented audit found overlapping routes and a misleading Emergency Care destination.
states.trade: This is a heuristic audit, not evidence from patient interviews.

states.title: Urgency becomes the first decision.
states.explain: The first split becomes Get Care Today or Schedule Your Care. This moves the burden of classification away from the patient.
states.trade: Cost and eligibility detail move into a deeper layer.
labels: How soon do you need care?

states.title: Put detail after direction, not before it.
states.explain: Once a route is chosen, care types can be compared using common dimensions: cost, wait and what they treat.
states.trade: Two sprints, a third-party API and no patient access limited validation.

title: Marriott Bonvoy SPOG
question: What must an associate read in one glance?
gap: Specification callouts and finished screens are separated, obscuring why some information earns the overview.

states.title: Separate scan, exception and detail.
states.explain: Arrivals and departures establish the shift. Operational exceptions require attention. Secondary metrics can wait in detail views.
states.trade: A single overview only works when some information is deliberately left out.

states.title: Reserve emphasis instead of coloring everything.
states.explain: The documented system combines neutral surfaces with a restrained gold accent. Weight, placement and shape carry hierarchy alongside color.
states.trade: A restrained palette offers fewer color shortcuts; hierarchy must do more work.

states.title: Keep enrolment over the work already open.
states.explain: The original modal keeps enrolment in the associate’s current context. A guided common path reduces the need to interpret a raw form while talking to a guest.
states.trade: The case study notes less flexibility for rare edge cases.

title: Encoded
question: How do you anchor an exhibition in a museum you cannot alter?
gap: Capture, alignment and activation clips are present, but the constraints that make the pipeline necessary are difficult to follow.

states.title: Use the phone as a production constraint.
states.explain: A normal visitor’s phone could capture the artworks without a rig or marker installation. Polycam was part of the capture workflow.
states.trade: Lighting and limited access produced inconsistent scans and repeat attempts.

states.title: Choose visual positioning for physical registration.
states.explain: The project describes Niantic Lightship VPS localization against the space. The choice avoids adding visible markers to the museum.
states.trade: A vendor map becomes an operational dependency. Thin coverage can mean drift or failure.

states.title: A successful activation is not a durability test.
states.explain: The site counts activations, while its next-steps section asks about dwell time and what happens when the gallery or map changes.
states.trade: Monitoring, recapture and dwell-time instrumentation are proposed next work, not shipped features.

title: Bodhi on Vision Pro
question: When does patience become an interface failure?
gap: The page shows the tree and gestures; the documented tradeoff between deliberate pauses and unclear recovery needs its own visual.

states.title: A pause can be part of the conversation.
states.explain: The thesis deliberately slows turn-taking to make the system feel patient. Attention and voice are the stated interaction focus.
states.trade: First encounters can interpret intentional silence as a stalled application.

states.title: Intentional silence and failure can look identical.
states.explain: If speech is misunderstood, an interface designed around presence provides few obvious ways to redirect it. The case study names this recovery gap.
states.trade: Archived prototypes include visible controls; do not present every iteration as literally control-free.

states.title: Expose recovery without abandoning the tone.
states.explain: Proposed state study: acknowledge a missed exchange and offer repeat, pause or exit. Test whether those choices remain discoverable during a quiet encounter.
states.trade: This is a new testable proposal. No validation or implementation claim.

title: Bloom installation
question: Should movement control the image, or influence it?
gap: A long archive of mandalas and room studies makes the slow mapping choice hard to distinguish from visual experimentation.

states.title: Immediate mapping encourages performance.
states.explain: The documented concern: one-to-one tracking turns the encounter into a mirror. Visitors start testing what each gesture does.
states.trade: The diagram models the idea, not the original algorithm or a measured signal.

states.title: Let movement affect growth over time.
states.explain: The case study describes MediaPipe body tracking influencing growth over seconds rather than frames. A slow response supports the intended atmosphere.
states.trade: The connection can become too subtle for visitors to recognize.

states.title: The room is part of the interface.
states.explain: The project documents a brighter room being harder to settle in, and identifies light and acoustics as design work that came too late.
states.trade: EEG media does not by itself establish that this design caused calm.

title: Mind Your Feelings
question: What makes a touch feel connected to a physical response?
gap: The kiosk and sculpture are visible, but the developer contribution between them is mostly confined to the reflection.

states.title: A feeling becomes a visible selection.
states.explain: A visitor selects an emotion and maps it on the body. The interaction needs a clear input state before its color travels to the sculpture.
states.trade: Avoid implying that a selected emotion is a diagnosis.

states.title: Trace the interaction across the system.
states.explain: The project names a JavaScript interface, Python bridge, and WLED / Arduino hardware system. This is the useful implementation chain to show.
states.trade: No protocol, timing benchmark or retry mechanism is documented here.

states.title: The physical output closes the loop.
states.explain: The sculpture responds in the selected color. A prompt response makes the relationship between the visitor’s action and the object legible.
states.trade: Connection-loss and reset behavior would need code or a recorded test before being shown as implemented.

title: AI Self
question: How did one research question lead to three different artifacts?
gap: Perception experiments, an AR concept and a VR build can read as one continuous product unless their evidence types are separated.
insert: At the transition into the first experiment.

states.title: Start with what the model names.
states.explain: The Cloud Vision experiments compare the meaning of personal photographs with the patterns the model identifies.
states.trade: The images are exploratory evidence, not a benchmark of model accuracy.

states.title: Turn the finding into a design question.
states.explain: Chaise asks what a pattern-reading presence would feel like beside someone all day. The source labels its AR walkthrough as idea conception.
states.trade: Treat the companion as a concept, not a deployed ambient AI.

states.title: Make the question spatial.
states.explain: The VR study imagines an AI assembling a world from what it inherited about humanity. Process sketches explain scene structure.
states.trade: This is an experiential prototype, not evidence of AI consciousness.

title: Naavo
question: What stays fixed when the product changes?
gap: The archive shows many packaging outcomes; the stronger process story is the relationship between identity, dosha coding and label hierarchy.

states.title: Build a human figure from a dosha vocabulary.
states.explain: The original construction sheet shows the relationship between the three doshas, simple forms and a unified human mark.
states.trade: This is the project’s identity logic, not a clinical model.

states.title: Separate the fixed lockup from variable content.
states.explain: The label construction specifies a shared hierarchy while product names and dosha identifiers change across the family.
states.trade: The source gives proportions; no new measurements are invented in this explanation.

states.title: Check the system on a different format.
states.explain: The incense pack carries the same identity and hierarchy in a tall printed format. Compare it with the oil label specification.
states.trade: Shelf legibility needs a real distance test; a mockup alone does not validate it.

title: Aananda
question: How does cultural research become a usable visual language?
gap: The cultural references, app and book arrive in separate blocks, making their relationship feel aesthetic rather than deliberate.
insert: Between the cultural references and app screens.

states.title: Begin with a source that can be interpreted.
states.explain: The project connects conversations with the designer’s father and Jain temple references to symbols, typography and illustration.
states.trade: Show these as the documented sources, not as formal user research.

states.title: Carry the language into a learning interface.
states.explain: The original app places learning and events inside the visual system. Compare which motifs become navigation, illustration or background.
states.trade: No usability study is documented; this visual analysis is retrospective.

states.title: Change the reading pace for print.
states.explain: The Ahimsa spread uses a large concept page beside a denser explanation. The hierarchy changes because a book supports sustained reading.
states.trade: Do not claim the same layout can simply be scaled from phone to paper.

title: Alpha Stockathon
question: What makes this a learning game instead of a themed lesson?
gap: Characters and screens dominate the archive. The connection between a financial concept, a decision and its consequence needs to be made explicit.
insert: Before the character and interface gallery.

states.title: Give the learner a reason to continue.
states.explain: The hero, dragon and Stock Baba give the project a narrative objective. Their role is to motivate movement through the lessons.
states.trade: Narrative interest is not evidence of learning effectiveness.

states.title: Teach through a decision and its consequence.
states.explain: The project describes simulated decisions across options, shorting and market cap. The diagram reconstructs that stated learning loop.
states.trade: The Figma prototype does not establish a production market simulator.

states.title: Separate the prototype from the claim.
states.explain: A three-day concept can demonstrate interaction design and visual scope. To claim learning, the next study would ask players to explain the concept after play.
states.trade: A learning assessment is proposed, not a result already obtained.

title: Cube of Creations
question: What remains the same when a character becomes interactive?
gap: The long film and game archive hides the core idea and makes the chronology difficult to follow.
insert: Before the film, with the archive below.

states.title: An insight changes the character’s form.
states.explain: The character begins as a square; collecting insights gives it another dimension. This is a narrative rule rather than a decorative transformation.
states.trade: The sketches document exploration, not a fixed original production plan.

states.title: In film, the author controls when change happens.
states.explain: The 2022 film sequences encounters and insights for the viewer. Pacing belongs to the authored edit.
states.trade: A viewer can interpret the story but cannot change its timing.

states.title: In a game, the player must carry the action.
states.explain: The 2021 2D game and 2024 Unreal work bring the character into playable space. Questions, distractions and Doubt become interaction material.
states.trade: These are separate iterations; the 2D game predates the film.

title: Broken and Beautiful
question: What turns a public prompt into participation?
gap: The stop-sign idea, QR entry and collected responses are spread through the page, so the participation mechanism is easy to miss.
insert: After the opening insight, before “The Stand”.

states.title: Borrow the stopping power of a familiar object.
states.explain: The case study describes a stop sign repurposed as an invitation. The design question is whether a passerby notices and understands the prompt.
states.trade: The response total does not reveal how many people walked past.

states.title: Keep the opening small enough to answer.
states.explain: One question asks what feels beautiful and what feels broken. The web interface lets people contribute without turning the encounter into a long survey.
states.trade: Anonymity and a short prompt shape the kind of responses collected.

states.title: Show the voices before summarizing them.
states.explain: The archive supports a shared reading of submitted thoughts. Word imagery can help explore themes, but should remain separate from participant quotations.
states.trade: 285+ responses and 15 interviews are totals, not a conversion funnel or representative sample.

title: Shot on iPhone
question: How much interaction can a photograph carry?
gap: The posters repeat the finished image; the design decision is the handoff from viewing a photograph to reading its story.

states.title: Let the photograph work without instructions.
states.explain: The self-initiated project responds to the campaign format by keeping the image as the first encounter.
states.trade: This is not an Apple commission.

states.title: Use the QR as an optional deeper layer.
states.explain: The documented mechanism opens the story behind the frame after a scan. Interaction is placed after the image, not in front of it.
states.trade: The QR destination must be checked separately before publication.

states.title: Stop before the interaction overwhelms the image.
states.explain: The reflection names simplicity as the constraint. More features would need to justify why they improve the image-to-story transition.
states.trade: No participation analytics or tested alternate flow is documented.

title: Illustrations / Apna Adda
question: What proves exploration without confusing it with the final identity?
gap: Independent series blend together, and the cube exploration was mistaken for the selected shop identity in earlier mockups.
insert: At the start of the Apna Adda subsection.

states.title: Show options as options.
states.explain: The cube and typographic variations demonstrate the exploration space. They should be captioned explicitly as explorations.
states.trade: Do not apply an exploration to a new object and imply it was selected.

states.title: Identify the direction used in the menu.
states.explain: The final menu is the strongest available evidence of the applied identity. Use its actual lettering and visual language when discussing the choice.
states.trade: The reason for rejecting individual alternatives is not documented; do not invent it.

states.title: Judge the identity by the task it supports.
states.explain: A useful next review would ask whether someone can find a food category, item and price quickly in the menu. This ties the identity to a real use.
states.trade: This is a proposed evaluation, not a completed usability test.

title: AI Experiments
question: What does the model change about the interface?
gap: Tool lists and visual reels obscure the causal chain from input to inference to a user-visible response.
insert: One expandable mechanism diagram beneath each experiment.

states.title: Start with the material the system receives.
states.explain: Each experiment uses a different input: a phrase, camera frame, public feed, drawing or conversation. The diagram connects that material to a visible behavior.
states.trade: The collection has 12 current entries. Runtime and privacy boundaries differ by project.

states.title: Name what happens between input and output.
states.explain: Distinguish inference, projection, rendering and designed fiction. A visual effect is not automatically a model output.
states.trade: Mechanisms below come from the current project descriptions; they are not new benchmarks.

states.title: Show the choice or uncertainty exposed to the user.
states.explain: A useful engineering story explains what the person can inspect, change or doubt when a model mediates the interaction.
states.trade: Do not claim every experiment is entirely local: Guise explicitly uses a server proxy.
